title: Without a lawsuit, Linux might not have happened
description: Did a UNIX lawsuit help Linux become the dominant operating-system kernel it is today? The history of BSD, Linux, and the early Internet makes for a fascinating read.

title: An updated Clairic and Clairic-flash are now open-weight, from the new Workers AI Superintelligence team
description: Add your teaser here. It should complement the headline, not repeat it. Teaser cannot be longer than 240 characters. The Blog Review Gem will suggest an excerpt. Clairic graduates from preview, while Clairic-flash joins the repertoire on Workers AI. We’re doing an open-weight rel…

title: Why We Changed Our Minds About New TLDs
description: After criticizing the 2014 new TLD expansion, a DNS industry veteran explains how AI agents, decentralized identity and emerging Internet protocols have changed his perspective on the potential value of new namespaces.

title: How IPv4 Became An Asset Class Most Technology Leaders Still Misread
description: IPv4 address space has become a traded asset with fluctuating prices, deployment costs and regional transfer restrictions. Infrastructure operators must reconsider how they acquire, lease and manage addresses as a scarce resource.

title: France’s Proposed DNS Blocks Draw Criticism Over Internet Access and Free Expression
description: French authorities considered DNS-level restrictions on major social media platforms during protests, raising concerns about technical effectiveness, collateral disruption to Internet access and the legal limits of government intervention.

title: How Cloudflare WAF helps protect against Java4Shell (CVE-2026-114938)
description: Java4Shell is a critical memory-corruption flaw in OpenJDK's Base64 decoder that can lead to remote code execution. Cloudflare has released six WAF managed rules for paid plans that logs matching requests by default. Patch your Java runtimes now.

title: Who’s Delivering GTA 6? A RIPE Atlas Measurement Story
description: How do you deliver a 200 GB game to millions of players? As GTA 6 pre-loads got underway last week, we turned to RIPE Atlas to examine how DNS and content delivery networks help PlayStation and Xbox share the load.

title: Grant Report: Markdown Support for GNU AutoGen
description: Network Time Foundation received a 2025 ARIN Community Grant to add Markdown output to GNU AutoGen, the tool that generates the NTP Project’s documentation. NTF President Harlan Stenn reports on what the team accomplished, what got in the way, and what comes next.

title: Quad9’s withdrawal from France: A canary in the coal mine
description: Quad9's forced withdrawal from France highlights the dangers of mandating DNS-level blocking. We explore why forcing public resolvers to act as content filters is technically flawed and threatens the open Internet.

title: IP for Africa, Not Africa for AFRINIC: An IP Address Has No Continent
description: Challenging AFRINIC's restrictions on IPv4 transfers, Lu Heng argues that regional registries should safeguard address records without controlling ownership, mobility or commercial rights, questioning whether geographic stewardship has become institutional authority.

title: Microsoft 365 Outage Raises Questions About Africa’s Digital Sovereignty
description: A Microsoft 365 disruption highlights Africa's dependence on foreign cloud platforms, raising questions about digital sovereignty, operational control and the infrastructure resilience needed to keep essential services running during outages.

title: ICANN Confirms 1,610 New gTLD Applications as Contention Falls Ahead of Evaluation
description: ICANN confirms 1,610 applications in its 2026 new gTLD round after replacement strings reduce contention. Public comments and formal objections are now open, with evaluation underway and key deadlines extending into March 2027.

title: Solar photovoltaics for Internet resilience (Part 2): Choosing suppliers and components
description: Guest Post: Choosing a solar PV supplier involves more than comparing prices. Ask the right questions about support, cybersecurity, system design, and installation quality to ensure your system remains reliable for years to come.

title: ICANN to Test FBI and INTERPOL Authentication Systems for Domain Registration Data Requests
description: ICANN will test FBI and INTERPOL identity systems to authenticate law enforcement requests for nonpublic domain registration data, supporting a future 24-hour response requirement for urgent disclosures.

title: DNS-OARC 47 Highlights Rising Query Volumes and Post-Quantum DNSSEC Challenges
description: Research presented at DNS-OARC 47 reveals rising DNS query duplication, obstacles to post-quantum DNSSEC deployment and unresolved delegation security questions, alongside new approaches to improving resolver performance and efficiency.

title: Why Later Trademarks and a Website Disclaimer Failed in a UDRP Dispute
description: A WIPO panel ordered two domain transfers after finding that later trademark registrations and corporate formation did not establish legitimate interests, while a website disclaimer failed to overcome evidence of bad-faith targeting.

title: How DNS Hosting Defaults Shape DNSSEC Adoption
description: A study of 257 million gTLD domains finds DNSSEC adoption concentrated among providers that enable signing by default, suggesting that DNS hosting practices and automated delegation management matter more than individual registrant decisions.

title: Hot topics in DNS from DNS OARC 47
description: Hot topics from two days of meetings about the current state of the DNS at OARC 47.

title: Kitesurf is now open source
description: Kitesurf, our experimental browser engine for AI agents, is now open source. Inspect the code, run it locally, or deploy your own instance on Cloudflare Workers.

title: Adapting to AI penetration testing orchestrators: The Modern Security Model
description: AI-orchestrated penetration testing platforms like ARTEX have become increasingly powerful tools enabling effective attacks on exposed infrastructure. Here we share Cloudflare’s observations and recommended countermeasures.

title: Introducing Spend Management: Spending limits and alerts for Cloudflare
description: Spend Management adds opt-in spending caps for Cloudflare Workers and Durable Objects, and more products soon. Here is how we built the metering pipeline that turns usage into runtime decisions.

title: Could pigeons deliver the Internet?
description: Guest Post: What happens when we replace network cables with carrier pigeons? We worked out how many birds you would need.

title: Post-Quantum Authentication: Lessons from Prague
description: In October, the Internet Architecture Board (IAB) held a two-day workshop in Prague with people who are deploying post-quantum authentication. These are the first impressions from the co-chairs, ahead of the full workshop report.

title: ARIN Online Achieves SOC 2 Compliance
description: ARIN has successfully completed an initial Service Organizational Control (SOC) 2 Type II audit of ARIN Online and renewed compliance for our Resource Public Key Infrastructure (RPKI) for the fourth year.

title: 2026 APNIC Survey: Executive Council Response
description: The 2026 APNIC Survey highlights strong confidence in APNIC’s services and the priorities of Members and stakeholders across the region.

title: [Podcast] Submarine cable resilience and economics
description: How resilient is the global submarine cable network? Geoff Huston explores its evolution, vulnerabilities, economics, and who has an interest in keeping it running.

title: What’s up with email at IETF 127
description: Email is the oldest widely used application on the Internet, but it continues to evolve. At IETF 127 four working groups will meet to improve the security and usability of mail, and two Birds-of-a-Feather sessions propose improvements in mail operations and the way users sign up …

title: Choosing QuePaxa, an unusual consensus algorithm
description: Cloudflare is building an experimental consensus service using a never-before-deployed consensus algorithm, QuePaxa. In this post we explain how QuePaxa works and why we chose it.

title: SIDN publishes RSSAC002 traffic metrics for .nl
description: Guest Post: SIDN Labs shares insight into traffic to the authoritative .nl nameservers.

title: The Machine Majority: What Bot Traffic Looks Like from Central Asia
description: Most web pages are now fetched by machines rather than people, at least on the networks we can measure. I pulled data for thirteen countries across Central Asia and the Caucasus to see what that looks like from our corner of the world, and what it means for those of us who run ne…

title: IETF Administration LLC 2027 Draft Budget
description: The IETF Administration LLC has prepared its draft budget for 2027 and now seeks community feedback.

title: Launching the Vite Ecosystem Fund
description: Cloudflare is distributing the first $301,300 of the Vite Ecosystem Fund to open source projects and maintainers. The recipients were chosen by a panel of Vite stack core team members, including maintainers not employed by Cloudflare.

title: Your Router Trusts Its Validator. But Who's Watching the Validator?
description: ROV turned your validator into a forwarding policy source. The registries have strengthened their side of the RPKI, but the chain from repository to router runs on your infrastructure. When that chain breaks, it often breaks silently.

title: The DOs and don’ts of post-quantum DNSSEC
description: Post-quantum signatures could dramatically enlarge DNSSEC responses, shifting many queries from UDP to TCP. Should resolvers limit unnecessary DNSSEC data, or is greater TCP use inevitable?

title: The post-quantum future of web privacy
description: Cryptographic protocols like Privacy Pass help keep web sites safe from abuse while keeping their users private. This post looks at the quantum threat to these protocols, and some new post-quantum cryptography that may help close the gap.

title: The Internet's New Factories
description: AI factories create several traffic systems at once, and power is shaping where they can be built. This article asks what operators can see, what stays private, and who decides how these systems are connected.

title: PCAP-LM: Helping AI assistants read network traffic
description: Guest Post: Packet captures are the ground truth of network operations, but analysing them is slow, requires specialist expertise, and does not scale. PCAP-LM rewrites captures into a form that AI assistants can read, helping address that mismatch.

title: Agents aren’t humans (but they kinda are)
description: AI agents act for millions, but servers see intermediaries that strip user visibility. This post defines the problem space and introduces a collaborative approach to safely identifying, allowing, and managing this automated traffic.

title: Do Registrars Use DNSSEC on Their Own Domains?
description: Registrars must support DNSSEC for customers, but how many use it themselves? A study of 698 registrar domains finds fewer than one in ten has a DS record, with European registrars ahead of the rest. Tobias Sattler explores the gap and its possible explanations.

title: The Internet didn’t break; we just forgot what it was leaning on
description: Guest Post: When international links fail, hidden dependencies can take local services with them. Here’s how operators can design for local resilience.

title: The RIPE Chair Team Reports - Highlights from RIPE 93
description: From digital independence and practical AI to inclusion and research, RIPE 93 gave the community plenty to discuss and act on. The RIPE Chair Team shares personal highlights from Sofia and ways to get involved in the work ahead.

title: Suggested IETF 127 Sessions for Getting Familiar with New Topics
description: These IETF 127 meeting sessions are likely to include discussions and proposals that are accessible to a broad range of Internet technologists whether they are new to the IETF or long-time participants.

title: SIDN Publishes RSSAC002 Traffic Metrics for .nl
description: SIDN Labs has released open DNS traffic data for .nl in the same format used by root server operators. In this guest post, they explain what they’re sharing and how it opens up new comparisons across the DNS.

title: RIPE 93 Daily Meeting Blog
description: RIPE 93 has kicked off in Sofia - city of wisdom, Roman ruins, and yellow brick roads. As always, you can view the slides, you can watch the recordings, but if you want to get to the bottom of what's really going on, read this daily meeting blog!

description: More local peering, stronger routing security and a shared ambition to improve connectivity: CAPIF 5 brought Central Asia’s Internet community to Dushanbe to compare progress, discuss persistent challenges and learn from the people building the region’s networks.

description: Prepare for the upcoming meeting with this look at the Draft Policies on the agenda at ARIN 58, taking place 22-23 October in Miami, Florida, and online.

description: Anyone can help shape the policies that govern Internet number resources in the ARIN region. Here’s how to submit a policy proposal, read a Draft Policy page, and make your voice heard at our next Public Policy and Members Meeting.

title: Get Ready for ARIN Elections
description: The 2026 ARIN Elections are approaching, making this a good time to review the process and the participation opportunities available to you and your organization. Here’s a step-by-step guide to help you prepare to cast your vote this fall.

title: New features for RFC-Editor.org
description: New features implemented on RFC-Editor.org aim to make the site more useful and engaging for RFC consumers.

description: A transition to a new modern, modular, and containerized infrastructure for email services provided for ietf.org, iab.org, irtf.org, rfc-editor.org (including email lists) was completed on 11 September 2026.

description: The Independent Series Editor (ISE) selection criteria survey is live and we welcome your input on the capabilities and expectations the IAB should consider when selecting a future ISE. Please respond by 11 October 2026.

description: Post-quantum key establishment has moved from standards into deployment. Post-quantum authentication has not moved nearly as far, and specification work is no longer the only constraint. The IAB is holding a workshop in Prague on 11 and 12 October 2026 to bring deployment experie…
